messages:
alice.h: Heads up — we've got an unexplained p95 spike for the /v1/generate endpoint in us-west-2 since ~09:30 UTC. Customer-facing latency up, some requests are getting queued in the ingress layer but not erroring.
ben_v: seeing same in dashboards — p95 jumped from 180ms -> 1.4s, p99 ~3.2s. Throughput steady, CPU on workers not fully saturated.
carmen: admission queue depth metric shows a sustained rise, worker queueing_time metric up. Looks like requests are piling at the frontdoor rather than failing fast.
miguel-oncall: tagging me. Any deploys or config changes around 09:20–09:35? deploy-bot: deploy redwood/runtime v3.12.1 to us-west-2 completed at 09:18 UTC (CI job 98321).
alice.h: no schema changes. runtime rollout was a canary->gradual. Canary looked fine. Spike aligns shortly after canary passed to 50% at 09:22.
ben_v: grabbing kube logs and metrics. Quick check: ingress-admit shows long tail in process_queue loop. Putting here a sample stack trace line from a worker log: `WARN request_dispatcher.go:312 handler blocked waiting on permit for 620ms`
carmen: also seeing many small delays for KV cache warmups right before queueing bursts. Could be concurrency fairness / permit leak on release path.
miguel-oncall: repro attempt — locally hit the endpoint with 200 rps bursts for 60s against canary and stable; canary shows higher queuing under same burst. Starting capture: `curl -sS http://internal-metrics/us-west-2/ingress?window=5m | jq .admit_queue`
ben_v: results of `kubectl top pods -n runtime --sort-by=cpu` shows workers not pegged; suggests blocking at admission gate. Checking permit counters: `redis-cli HGETALL admit:permits:us-west-2` — many permits in 'leased' status and stale owner IDs.
alice.h: that points to a permit-release race, possibly introduced by the v3.12.1 change in the async flush path.
carmen: quick mitigation we can try: toggle admission control conservative mode to prefer rejections over queueing. Patch deployed to toggle `admit.max_queue_ms=250` and `admit.reject_on_full=true` in us-west-2 config.
miguel-oncall: applying config patch now to us-west-2 (temp). Command: `rdctl config set region.us-west-2.admit.reject_on_full=true && rdctl config set region.us-west-2.admit.max_queue_ms=250`
deploy-bot: config roll 4578 applied to us-west-2; change will propagate to 3/3 control nodes.
ben_v: after toggle p95 dropped back to ~220ms within 90s, p99 down to ~600ms. Queue depth normalized. Customers calling in still at first-party pace but looks better.
alice.h: OK mitigation confirms problem in queueing policy. We should roll back the permit code change from v3.12.1 and add stronger tests.
carmen: for short term we should also add a cleanup task that reclaims stale leased permits older than 2s. I'll open a PR.
miguel-oncall: action items: 1) revert permit-release change (eng-runtime), 2) add permit reaper job (eng-sre), 3) add e2e burst test asserting no queueing regressions (devex), 4) communicate to affected customers.
ben_v: I filed INCIDENT-4021 with notes and attached metric graphs + heap of logs. Adding owners: @alice.h, @carmen, @miguel-oncall.
alice.h: customer comms draft: "We observed transient latency regressions due to admission queueing after a runtime rollout. We applied a config mitigation to prioritize fast failures while we fix the root cause. We’re rolling back the change and will follow up with a postmortem." Will post to CS.
carmen: small repro snippet for QA to validate fix: ```bash
# burst test against canary
for i in {1..60}; do seq 1 200 | xargs -n1 -P200 curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}\n" http://canary.us-west-2.internal/v1/generate; sleep 1; done
```
miguel-oncall: leaving this thread but will follow-up in the incident doc. If anyone sees requeues again, ping me. :thumbsup:
alice.h: thanks all — marking as active incident until revert and PR merged.
